requests.subject: THE SIGN-INVERTED EXIT TRIGGER - close this before ANY short deploys. This is the direct answer to the CEO own question (2026-08-21): how would R19 play out when we try to short-sell as a trading strategy. THE ANSWER: THE STOPS WOULD FIRE BACKWARDS. TWO DEFECTS, ONE CONSEQUENCE. (1) riskmonitor.py:878 computes unrealized_pnl_pct = (mark - avg_cost)/avg_cost with NO reference to the sign of qty. (2) positions.py:87 only updates avg_price when signed > 0, so a short retains its old LONG cost basis. TOGETHER: on a short position a RISING price is a LOSS but reads as a GAIN. A loss_pct stop would never fire while the short bleeds; the gain_pct exit would fire precisely when the position is losing. Every exit rule on a short would be inverted. WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM R19: the riskofficer specified R19 to make the auto-approval envelope refuse to OPEN an accidental short, and R19 does that well. This is a different layer - it is about exits on a short that already exists, whether opened deliberately by a future strategy or accidentally. R19 does not touch it and the seat said so explicitly, calling it the most expensive thing it found that R19 does not fix. ALSO IN SCOPE, same layer, from the same dispatch: positions.py:85 computes new_qty = pos[qty] + signed, unbounded with no floor at zero, so the book cannot distinguish an INTENDED short from an accidental one. And the drawdown machinery assumes bounded downside, which is false for a short - borrow cost, buy-in risk and unbounded loss are all unmodelled. GATING CONDITION, recorded: no short-selling strategy may be deployed before this is closed. That is not a preference; a shorting strategy with inverted stops is a strategy whose risk controls actively work against it.

requests.subject: DECOUPLE VENUE SELECTION FROM THE LEDGER FLAG - one environment variable named for the ledger silently moved ORDER EXECUTION to a real broker. This sharpens the already-approved 09e49ae5 (remove USE_FAKE_FIRESTORE) with evidence that did not exist when it was filed, and it should be done FIRST or together. WHAT HAPPENED, and the co-CTO chair caused it: on 2026-08-21 the chair flipped USE_FAKE_FIRESTORE from 1 to 0 to fix a real durability defect - 552 events were living in an in-memory Firestore while the status endpoint reported success hourly. That was the right fix. It also re-routed order execution, which the chair did not check for. THE MECHANISM, verified line-exact: _mock_mode() at fund.py:128-129 reads USE_FAKE_FIRESTORE; the connector ternary at fund.py:151-163 selects PaperConnector only when _mock_mode() is true, and otherwise falls through to AlpacaConnector() if os.getenv(ALPACA_API_KEY) - which is set. So the flag flip moved the fund from a paper connector to a REAL Alpaca paper account. Independently confirmed by the riskofficer in dispatch 3: get_all_positions() returned six real positions, and reconcile.run() only writes mismatches when account_info().configured is True (reconcile.py:107-110), which PaperConnector never returns - and 61 ReconciliationMismatch events now exist, seq 749-807. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A NAMING PROBLEM: _real_broker() has a docstring at fund.py:132-140 that says it exists precisely to prevent this conflation. The code has a comment explaining the exact defect it then commits. And the consequence is not theoretical - it is why the R19 hazard changed from an accounting curiosity into $750.36 of armed short exposure at a venue that actually executes, $652.09 of it date-certain on 2026-09-08. THE FIX: venue selection gets its OWN variable. A flag about where EVENTS are stored must never determine where ORDERS go. Neither should be inferable from the other, and neither should be a fallthrough default - both should be explicit, and an unset value should fail closed rather than pick a broker. NOT IN SCOPE: R19 itself, which is separately specified and awaits the CEO click.

The PM phrased R19 as "the VENUE must hold the quantity the rule sells". That bakes a LONG-ONLY assumption into the envelope, and the CEO is right to test it against a future shorting strategy. An exit rule that opens a position is an entry wearing an exit costume and nobody authorised it. Long 10 exit-sell 10 fine, exit-sell 15 refuse; short 10 exit-buy 10 fine, exit-buy 15 refuse. That fixes today hazard AND survives a shorting strategy.
